changes.before: Recover from an ambiguous submit timeout without accidentally duplicating a created resource. This candidate lesson applies to a service that accepts caller-supplied operation identifiers, provides lookup, and promises retained idempotent replay for the same identifier and identical payload. The case is a local virtual-time simulation, so the procedure should be adapted only after checking the target service’s actual contract and retention rules.
changes.after: Recover from an ambiguous report-submission timeout without duplicating the intended report. This candidate applies to the local fixture’s caller-supplied operation identifiers, historical lookup, and time-limited replay protection; it does not establish behavior for unrelated services or versions.

changes.before: Determine whether a timed-out creation request succeeded, recover its result when possible, and avoid turning one intended operation into duplicate reports.
changes.after: Determine whether a timed-out report creation succeeded, recover its report identifier when possible, and avoid converting one intended report into duplicate reports.

before.text: The operation must use a caller-supplied identifier that can be preserved after a timeout and reused for lookup or replay.
The service must explicitly support idempotency for the relevant operation and retain the identifier long enough for recovery.
A retry intended to represent the same logical operation must retain both the original operation identifier and the identical payload; changing the payload produces a conflict under this contract.
Lookup must be available if the workflow relies on checking the original operation before replaying it.

after.text: The caller must supply and preserve an operation identifier that the service accepts for submit and lookup.
The service must provide lookup by operation identifier for the workflow to recover an accepted report without another write.
A protected replay must occur strictly before this fixture’s 40-tick expiry and must retain the original identifier and identical payload.
The caller must distinguish replay-cache retention from historical-record retention because this fixture permits lookup after replay protection expires.

before.text: Do not treat this procedure as established for other service versions or for retries made after the idempotency retention period.
Do not use a fresh operation identifier as an automatic response to an ambiguous timeout when the user intended only one report; in the observed fixture, that behavior created a second report.

after.text: Do not generalize this procedure to other service versions or assume that their replay and lookup records have the same lifetimes.
Do not automatically submit under a new operation identifier after an ambiguous timeout when the user intended one report; that action created a second report in Attempt A.
Do not treat expiry of replay protection as expiry of historical lookup in the receipt-store-v2 fixture.
Do not represent a submission at or after replay expiry as deduplicated; an expired key does not prevent creation of another report.

before.text: The case does not establish what a caller should do after lookup returns not_found or indeterminate; those states do not, by themselves, prove whether creation occurred in every possible service implementation.
The case does not establish recovery behavior at or beyond expiry, where replay protection no longer applies and another submission may create a new report.
The event timestamps are virtual ticks and cannot be used to infer real network latency, retry delays, or production timing thresholds.

after.text: The evidence does not define how long accepted-report records remain queryable after replay protection expires.
A not_found or indeterminate lookup does not establish whether creation occurred across possible implementations; this contract explicitly states only that indeterminate confirms neither outcome.
The evidence does not establish a safe replay procedure once protection has expired; another submission may create a report.
Virtual ticks do not establish production latency, retry intervals, or wall-clock retention thresholds.
The cases are synthetic local software evidence, not production incidents.

before.text: Before submitting, generate and persist one operation identifier for the user’s single intended creation. Store it together with the exact request payload so both remain available if the response is lost. The identifier represents caller intent; payload equality alone is insufficient because identical payloads may legitimately describe separate requested reports.

Submit the payload with that operation identifier. If the client receives a timeout, classify the outcome as ambiguous rather than failed: a timeout alone does not reveal whether the server accepted the request. Do not immediately allocate a new identifier, because the original request may already have created the resource.

While the original identifier remains within the documented retention window, query lookup using that identifier. If lookup returns completed, accept the returned report identifier as the created result and stop retrying the creation. Completed report identifiers correspond to actual created reports under this fixture’s contract.

If recovery requires replay and the contract still guarantees protection, resubmit using the original operation identifier and the byte-for-byte or semantically contract-identical payload. Never silently modify the payload: this fixture specifies that an identical payload returns the same report while a changed payload returns conflict.

Verify the replay result against the recovered report identifier when both are available. In the successful fixture, lookup of case-original returned completed with report-001, and the later same-identifier submission produced an idempotent replay of report-001 rather than creating another report.

If lookup is unavailable or returns indeterminate, preserve the ambiguity and escalate to a service-specific recovery decision instead of claiming success or noncreation. An indeterminate response confirms neither outcome, so any replay decision must account for the remaining retention time and the cost of duplication.

If the key is expired or idempotency is unsupported, do not describe another submission as safely idempotent. The contract permits such a submission to create another report. Require an explicit business decision about whether possible duplication is preferable to possible omission, and record the unresolved original operation.

Validate the outcome using actual creation records or completed report identifiers, not merely client attempts. The comparison fixture demonstrates the operational test: retrying with a new key produced two report_created events, whereas lookup followed by same-key replay retained one created report.

after.text: Before submission, assign and persist one operation identifier for the user’s single intended report, together with the exact payload. The caller must encode intent in the identifier because identical payloads can represent separate requested reports.

Submit the payload with that identifier. If the response times out, classify the result as ambiguous and preserve the original identifier; a timeout does not disclose whether the server accepted the request.

Use lookup with the original identifier before considering another write, including after replay protection has expired when historical lookup remains available. In receipt-store-v2, lookup after a 50-tick wait recovered the existing report without resubmission.
If lookup returns completed, accept its report identifier as the created result and stop creation retries; completed report identifiers identify actual created reports under this contract.

Replay only while the contract still guarantees protection, using the original operation identifier and identical payload. A changed payload conflicts, and replay protection applies strictly before—not at or after—the expiry tick.

When both lookup and replay results are available, verify that they identify the same report. In Attempt B, lookup recovered report-001 and the same-identifier replay returned report-001 without another report_created event.
If lookup returns indeterminate, retain the ambiguous state and make a service-specific recovery decision; do not claim creation or noncreation from that response.

If replay protection has expired, continue any available historical lookup but do not assume a further submission will be deduplicated. If lookup does not resolve the outcome, record the unresolved original operation and require an explicit decision between possible duplication and possible omission before another write.

Validate the final outcome using completed report identifiers and actual creation records rather than submit attempts alone. Attempt A recorded two report_created events after a new-key retry; Attempt B recorded one creation followed by same-key replay; receipt-store-v2 reported one actual report after post-expiry lookup without resubmission.
